messages:
maria: Hey team — customer 'GlyphAI' reports streaming sessions randomly end with a broken pipe. They say client shows EOF and our billing UI marked those as 5xx. They provided a heap of logs, small repro. Anyone seen this pattern lately? :thinking:

alex: Noticed similar traces last month but usually proxy half-close or lingering-conn behavior. Can you paste the raw gateway header/log snippet?

maria: Pasted snippet from their gateway logs inline:

```
2026-02-14T18:02:03.112Z gateway-12345 INFO client_conn=open id=abcd1234
2026-02-14T18:02:07.234Z gateway-12345 WARN write_error err=write tcp 10.2.1.5:443->10.10.4.6:52310: write: broken pipe
2026-02-14T18:02:07.235Z gateway-12345 INFO stream_end cause=client_eof id=abcd1234
2026-02-14T18:02:07.236Z billing-svc INFO charge_class=5xx id=abcd1234
```

maria: They call it out as reproducible when they put a proxy in front of our endpoint that reuses keepalive connections and sometimes sends a TCP FIN before reading trailing chunked data.

alex: Hmm. Does our EOF/5xx heuristic treat a client half-close as gateway error? I thought we had a transient rule to avoid billing 5xx on client-abort.

jordan: We do have an EOF heuristic: if connection closed before any bytes received we mark as client_abort, else if our runtime saw a write fail we mark as 5xx. Edge case if proxy does halfclose after sending final chunk footers we may see write fail in runtime.

maria: Customer's reproduction steps (they provided):
1) Start long-lived streaming request to /v1/stream with chunked transfer-encoding
2) After 6s the upstream proxy sends FIN while app is still streaming trailers
3) Runtime logs write: broken pipe and request gets a 502 logged then billing shows 5xx

sam: Can you try to repro internally with curl and a simple netcat proxy that half-closes? I can spin something up.

maria: Provided a quick curl example from them:
```
curl -v -N -H "Transfer-Encoding: chunked" -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/stream --data-binary @payload.txt
```
Then they run a tiny Go proxy that forwards and calls conn.CloseWrite() early.

alex: Repro plan: replicate proxy behavior with socat/nc and verify our gateway sees a write errno and how we tag it. Also check if prefix/KV flush timing matters (i.e., if runtime already flushed token frames then write fail vs if not).

jordan: Quick note: we map certain socket errors to client_abort in meter when errno==ECONNRESET and remote closed without us returning 5xx. But write: broken pipe (EPIPE) path currently flows through runtime as a downstream write failure and we classify as 5xx.

maria: Customer is asking to unbill these as 5xx if it's provable that their proxy initiated FIN. They provided pcap showing FIN from client side.

billing: @maria, please open a support ticket with the pcap and mark "billing review". We'll pause automatic charge on the samples while engineering confirms classification.

ops-bot: New incident created: INC-2026-2043 - streaming-brokenpipe-billing (priority=P3)

sam: I reproduced locally with a Go proxy that calls CloseWrite after sending last chunk headers. I see the same sequence: our runtime errors on write and responds 502. I can attach the minimal repro.

alex: Thanks Sam — can you drop the repro gist into #eng-runtime and tag me? I want to trace through our socket wrapper. If we can reliably detect remote FIN-before-trailer we could remap EPIPE->client_abort for streaming endpoints only.

jordan: Caveat: remapping blindly could hide genuine gateway failures where our runtime truly failed to produce a response. We should gate by: 1) connection had prior bytes from client (i.e., chunk body completed) AND 2) client sent FIN before we closed write AND 3) runtime error is EPIPE/EINVAL. If all true, mark meter as client_abort.

maria: Customer wants ETA on resolution and possible retro-bill adjustments. Billing requested at least a short-term exemption for the sample IDs.

billing: We'll hold charges for sample IDs sent and await eng confirmation. If eng confirms heuristic change, we'll run a small backfill for the last 24h.

alex: Action items:
- sam: upload repro and test variations (CloseWrite vs FIN after trailers) — due EOD today.
- jordan: draft safe heuristic and unit tests, flag possible false-negatives — due tomorrow morning.
- maria: collect customer pcap + sample IDs and create billing ticket (thanks) — please link INC-2026-2043.

maria: Thanks, folks. I'll update customer with the incident link and that engineering is investigating. :thumbsup:

sam: Repro gist uploaded to #eng-runtime (link) — minimal Go proxy + curl steps. Verified EPIPE on write appears consistently when proxy half-closes.

alex: I'll pick this up after reviewing repro. If we can assert proxy-initiated FIN we should avoid 5xx billing. But need unit tests to avoid regression.

maria: Leaving this thread active — will post customer follow-ups.
